## Current Code Workflow (from code analyzer)
# Model Overview (for Diagnosis)
The probes expect one BERT4Rec network per category, accessed through `ModelView`. Relevant hooks are `item_emb`, `encode_sequence`, `score_candidates`, `log2feats`, and `predict_score`. Encoder implementation is not supplied. Inference histories are left-padded, truncated to L−1 items, and followed by a reserved mask token. The final sequence representation is `encode_sequence(tokens)[:, -1]`; candidate scores use its dot product with item embeddings.

# Diagnosis Inputs & Hooks
`DiagnosisProbe(view, device)` reads the actual network from `view.model` and public training histories from `view.user_train`. `run_full_diagnosis(train_loader)` switches to evaluation/inference mode and restores module modes and Python, NumPy, and Torch RNG states afterward.

Consumed records are sought on the loader, view, then network. At most four captured batches are replayed; the production iterator is never advanced. Margin probes call `view.log2feats(sequence)` and `view.predict_score(features, stacked_items)`.

# Probes & Metrics
- **Integrity:** Checks reserved-mask IDs, observed inference tokens, finite scores, live score agreement, padding invariance, and incorrect-readout controls. Explicit failures block history sensitivity; missing checks remain unavailable.
- **Consumed-pipeline audit:** Reconstructs crops, event positions, masks, labels, and seeded negatives from histories. When captured logits exist, recomputes CE/BPR terms and scalar reduction. Agreement supports bounded consistency, not gradient correctness.
- **Embedding collapse:** Maps mean pairwise catalog-embedding cosine to [0,1]. Values near 1 indicate angular alignment; approximately 0.5 indicates average cosine near zero. Neither alone establishes recommendation quality.
- **Masked-target margins:** Reports mean, tenth percentile, negative-beats-positive rate, and margin-below-0.5 rate. Larger margins and lower error rates indicate stronger training-target separation.

# Perturbation & Tests
Structural fixtures cover empty, short, full-length, and repeated-item histories. Tests perturb padding embeddings and right context, omit the mask, and use an incorrect count−1 readout. Audit calibration injects verified label/mask faults with reversible restoration and clean controls.

History sensitivity uses up to 200 users’ last training events. It deletes or masks oldest/newest blocks, comparing scores, ranks, HR@10, margins, and top-10 overlap against frozen candidates across three draws. Reports include bootstrap intervals and repeat/explore, length, and popularity strata.

# MODEL_DIAGNOSIS Schema & Limitations
Output contains `metrics` and `metric_definitions`, including `bert4rec_integrity`, `consumed_pipeline_audit`, collapse/margin statistics, and `training_history_sensitivity`. Missing observations carry nulls, counts, and reasons. Training recovery is not held-out generalization; interventions do not establish causal preferences. Fresh-process predictor parity, complete gradient wiring, attention-mask inspection, and four-category macro validation remain uncertified. Unavailable item-category metadata leaves breakdowns empty.

## Current Code Workflow (from code analyzer)
# Model Overview (for Diagnosis)
The probes expect one BERT4Rec network per category, accessed through `ModelView`. Relevant hooks are `item_emb`, `encode_sequence`, `score_candidates`, `log2feats`, and `predict_score`. Encoder implementation is not supplied. Inference histories are left-padded, truncated to L−1 items, and followed by a reserved mask token. The final sequence representation is `encode_sequence(tokens)[:, -1]`; candidate scores use its dot product with item embeddings.

# Diagnosis Inputs & Hooks
`DiagnosisProbe(view, device)` reads the actual network from `view.model` and public training histories from `view.user_train`. `run_full_diagnosis(train_loader)` switches to evaluation/inference mode and restores module modes and Python, NumPy, and Torch RNG states afterward.

Consumed records are sought on the loader, view, then network. At most four captured batches are replayed; the production iterator is never advanced. Margin probes call `view.log2feats(sequence)` and `view.predict_score(features, stacked_items)`.

# Probes & Metrics
- **Integrity:** Checks reserved-mask IDs, observed inference tokens, finite scores, live score agreement, padding invariance, and incorrect-readout controls. Explicit failures block history sensitivity; missing checks remain unavailable.
- **Consumed-pipeline audit:** Reconstructs crops, event positions, masks, labels, and seeded negatives from histories. When captured logits exist, recomputes CE/BPR terms and scalar reduction. Agreement supports bounded consistency, not gradient correctness.
- **Embedding collapse:** Maps mean pairwise catalog-embedding cosine to [0,1]. Values near 1 indicate angular alignment; approximately 0.5 indicates average cosine near zero. Neither alone establishes recommendation quality.
- **Masked-target margins:** Reports mean, tenth percentile, negative-beats-positive rate, and margin-below-0.5 rate. Larger margins and lower error rates indicate stronger training-target separation.

# Perturbation & Tests
Structural fixtures cover empty, short, full-length, and repeated-item histories. Tests perturb padding embeddings and right context, omit the mask, and use an incorrect count−1 readout. Audit calibration injects verified label/mask faults with reversible restoration and clean controls.

History sensitivity uses up to 200 users’ last training events. It deletes or masks oldest/newest blocks, comparing scores, ranks, HR@10, margins, and top-10 overlap against frozen candidates across three draws. Reports include bootstrap intervals and repeat/explore, length, and popularity strata.
